segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have real conversations in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. You can find a video of this podcast and find a worksheet to help you learn on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello Beth, how are you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you. How are you, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very happy. The sun is shining today.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: It is. It's a beautiful day.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What are we talking about?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Today we're talking about our childhoods.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So we'll talk about life, how it was, what our lives were like when we were children.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How interesting. Let's get started.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, Neil, what do you remember most about your childhood?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, it was such a long time ago.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But I can remember things, obviously, quite clearly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I lived in a different country when I was a child.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Where did you live?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I lived in Canada until I was 10 years old.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So I can remember very hot, humid summers,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: but very long and very cold and snowy winters.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So you always made snowmen, I guess, and had snowball fights.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes we always had a white Christmas which is great And I don think I ever had a white Christmas in England not in the south of England

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: well I moved house or my family moved house when I was 10 so I feel like a slightly

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: similar thing where all of my childhood memories really are in this house and playing with my

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: friends that lived in that village and went to my primary school when I lived in that house

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: having friends over for tea. That's a lot of strong memories of my childhood.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And what kind of things did you do when you were a child? What kind of hobbies and interests did

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: you have?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, my friends and I used to always put on shows. We would do gymnastics shows in the

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: garden. We'd say, Mum, Dad, come and watch my gymnastics show with my friend. We used to do

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: singing concerts. We wrote our own songs. Once my friend and I recorded onto a tape. Do you

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: remember tapes?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Of course I remember tapes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We recorded our own song onto a tape and we sent

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: it to a recording studio in the hope that they would sign us.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Is it a good song?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: It's great.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think we need to hear it.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Maybe at the end of the show.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: what about you what sort of hobbies did you have when you were a child

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I just remember playing outside a lot with my friends and having adventures and also doing lots and lots of sport so I always liked football and cricket And I played when I was in Canada I played ice hockey

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Ah, that's cool.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Can you still ice skate?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm okay.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'd say I'm better than most British people.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Because you grow up in Canada skating.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But I'm not brilliant.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: How do you think the world has changed since you were a child?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: The world is really different from when I was a child because when I was growing up we didn't have the internet or mobile phones and I think they've made such a difference to the way people communicate with each other.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And it drives me mad sometimes because my son would try to arrange to go out with his friends just to go to the park in a group chat.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And then nothing ever happens.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I just say, just go there.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It's 100 metres down the road.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Knock the door.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But I don't think that happens anymore.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think for me, like something that's really changed is like I was saying about tapes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: like the idea of playing a tape

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: or putting a CD in a CD player

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: like brings back amazing memories

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I used to have a CD that I would play

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and then I'd sing really loudly

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and I would imagine that then suddenly the band would be in the garden and they be there singing with me But I think those physical music devices even like having a video or a DVD like they bring back loads of memories

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: for me.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's recap the language we heard in our conversation about childhood, starting with

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: childhood, which is the period of time when you are a child.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We had memory a memory is something that you can remember from the past.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We can say that something brings back memories, which just means that it

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: reminds you of something that happened in the past.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And when we talk about things in the past, we often use the past simple.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: For example, I said that I played in the street with my friends.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we also heard used to and would, which is used when we talk about things that happened

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: a number of times in the past. So, for example, I used to play ice hockey. It means I played

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: ice hockey a lot and now I don't anymore.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And that's it for this episode of Real Easy English. Why not test what you've learnt with

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Join us next time when we'll be talking about Days Out.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Thanks for joining us and goodbye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye!
